analysis.title: CIO View: Global equities
key_insights: UBS CIO downgraded global equities to Neutral. It describes this as a more balanced risk-reward, not a bearish outlook. Absolute view Neutral, relative preference In line versus other asset classes.
Advice is to stay invested but diversify. Use periods of strength and volatility to rebalance concentrated positions and broaden exposure rather than add broad equity beta.

US equities downgraded to Neutral. S&P 500 targets are 8,000 for June 2027 and 8,200 for December 2027, which still imply further upside. The 10 largest companies are just shy of 40% of the index, so returns are more sensitive to a small group of companies.
Much of the AI infrastructure buildout planned for 2027 is already committed. UBS expects AI investment to rise from about USD 1.0tr in 2026 to USD 1.4tr in 2027.

The Eurozone remains Attractive. Revenue growth is accelerating, margins are recovering and earnings revisions are positive. UBS now expects Eurozone earnings growth of 20% in 2026 and 15% in 2027. Higher bond yields weigh on valuations.

Japan, Emerging Markets, Taiwan and Asia ex-Japan are moved from Attractive to Neutral. Reasons are AI monetization questions and possible capex moderation beyond 2027, which raise uncertainty for markets with large AI supply chain exposure.

The key AI uncertainty is shifting to 2028. Financing could become more selective if monetization is slower, and power generation, grid connectivity, equipment availability and permitting could limit infrastructure expansion. AI also raises disruption risk for incumbents, so the risk includes AI succeeding while widening the gap between leaders and laggards.

UBS favors quality within AI: capacity already in operation, visible AI revenues, strong balance sheets and internally funded investment. It also favors AI-resilient quality stocks (ARQ), plus industrials and health care, for earnings drivers less dependent on AI capex.
MSCI ACWI targets: 1,425 for June 2027 and 1,460 for December 2027, from 1,335 on 9 Nov 2026. Scenario targets for December 2027 are 1,680 (upside) and 1,000 (downside).

risk_factors: Strong profitability is increasingly reflected in expectations, so the bar for companies to deliver is rising.
Market concentration in the 10 largest US companies.
AI monetization may be slower than expected, with a possible moderation in capex beyond 2027.
Power generation, grid connectivity, equipment availability and permitting could limit AI infrastructure expansion.
AI disruption of incumbents' businesses and profit pools.
Higher bond yields weigh on equity valuations.
Downside scenario risks include an AI capex decline, US growth slowdown, geopolitical escalation, retaliatory tariffs and systemic cyber attacks.
vol_and_positioning: The 10 largest companies are just shy of 40% of the S&P 500, so index returns are more sensitive to a small group of firms.
UBS suggests using volatility and market strength to rebalance concentrated positions rather than adding beta.
geopolitical: Upside scenario: the Middle East conflict resolves and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire is reached.
Downside scenario: the Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts intensify.
US tariffs: the downside scenario has the US keeping a high effective tariff rate after the midterm elections, with trading partners retaliating more.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment rises from about USD 1.0tr in 2026 to USD 1.4tr in 2027, much of the 2027 buildout is already committed, and the upside scenario has ACWI at 1680 by December 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Slower monetization could make financing more selective, and power and permitting limits could slow the buildout. The downside scenario has ACWI at 1000 by December 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A moderation in AI capital spending beyond 2027, or monetization developing more slowly than expected.
